questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: academic opportunities, i wanted to add outdoor and leadership to my bachelor, wich of both i could get through NIH. Also i had heard from teacher and campus headmaster, that the studieeverimont og education kvality was high. Together with this i know about Norways, opportunities with it's nature for outdoor, and also the culture wich let you get the fully experience and ups the learning outcome

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Epic, very glad i did it, even though very difficult to leave a girlfriend at home

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: easy due to the exchangeoffice on NIH

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: got a site with information (canvas) from the exchange office and furthermore they where always there to help - on top we had a weekend with activities arranged by a NIH-student

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: if you pay a resonal amount of money, NIH get you on a housing list wich (with some critias) garanty you to get student housing to a fair price

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: choose SIO Kringsjå - very nice to live in house 200-500m from the school, wich have a lot of awsome facilities

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: easy to get help

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: i choose a corse pack from home i long time advance, and then later i confirmed the courses - it is also possibel (if not choosing outdoor) to choose specifik curses.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: the exhange office was always ready to help, via mail og by showing up at the office. Very friendly and often quick response (sometimes same day)

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I registrered for excactly the classes i wantet, wouldn't change a thing about that

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I advice to give attention that some curses is online and for my opinion it don't make a lot of sense to take online classes during exchange

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: im in third (6. semester last year) of my bachelor, and went on exhange to NIH where i and a few other students joined a norwegien class who was on second year (4. semester). The class was taught in english. but knowing Norwegian is a plus

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The outdoor studies differ from all other classes. In outdoor we were in a class and had 2 courses (classes) with more og less the same people in both classes. So you got near the teacher and your classmates, and possible for dialog wich was nice. Around half of all hours is active learning where you are outside and do something practical sometimes just half a day other times a week long trip

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
FRI213-1 Adventurous Learning and Skill Development
FRI214-1 Journeys Leadership and HSE

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
if you ejoy outdoor and would like to develop as a leader i recommend the to courses i had. Both are very practicel, vere FRI214 has a bit more reading than FRI213 but neither has a lot. 214 is focusd on you as a leader alone or in a group while being outdoor. where 213 is more focus on learning a selfchoosen skill while understading learning theores and pedogogic aspecst of outdoor learning. 
213 is build around a selfchosen projekt that centers around the 1-2 choosen outdoor skills

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: i enden up buying more outdoor ecupment than anticipated, and then i enden up with cooking as a projekt wich i used a lot of money on. And then traveling around and experiencing norway can be expensive but worth it

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: i have been to norway before and knew that it is very expensive espaccely foodwise. but due to low rate compared to DKK i wasn't as bad as i had anticipated.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: several social gruops where exchange students are more than welcome.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: An outdoor group, an sportsclub with 3 weekly activities, and a party group, though NIH for free. and several other sports and creative clubs though SIO (the housing) for a student friendly price

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: the activities lead by the NIH-students - you learn your fellow students better both classmates and cross classes.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go and do trips to DNT-cabins they are cheap and located cool places

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: for me being danish it was very easy since most is simelar

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: do activities with the NIH groups such as trips even if they are a bit expensive it's worth it espescely in the start. And try to socalise more with the norwegians if you want to learn more about culture and want some deeper connections even though it takes a bit more effort than connecting with the other exhange students. Hang out with the exhange students if you ejoy partying, and having the stupid kind of fun

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: none

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer:
The outdoor, how normal it is and the easy accesability to nature. Also the trust to people and the systems build on trust
when you first get close to a norwegian you can get very close, and really feel there friendlyness.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Enjoy it and don't think about how many money you use, it is worth it. And it will cost you a lot also more than the money you get from Erasmus

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer:
NIH let you borrow a few items for you housing for exampel ruters and clothhangers 
It is not neccesarry at all to speak norwegian but it's a big plus

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: focusing on the classes and socialising with the norwegians more than the exchange students

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: being away from my girlfriend how had a very difficult time being home alone

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
